title: VPA output to pitch plate -- grip length

joint.zone_note: Jeff located this joint as 'sheet 5, zone C10 (middle-left, lower)'. The DETAIL X caption prints at zone B10 on the 2026-JUL-23 POST export, with the view body immediately above it -- consistent.
joint.description: 0.250-28 bolt through the VPA output rod end into the mating flange, castellated nut + cotter pin retained, with a countersunk washer under the head.

provenance.column_I_caveat: In this block the workbook's comments column is a LOOSE HARDWARE LIST, not row-aligned: I62 (NAS77A4-015) sits on the header row and I64 (MS21299C4K) sits next to 'spherical bearing'. MS21299C4K is a countersunk washer, and its .063 +/-.006 in thickness matches the 'under head chamfer washer' at E67 exactly -- so I64 labels row 67, not row 64. Do not read column I positionally here.

elements.name: straight bushing
elements.note: Same 0.1875 in nominal as the tan-link bushing but a DIFFERENT tolerance band (4.71/4.81 vs 4.63/4.76) -- a different part, for the .250 in bolt.

source_ref.note: NAS77A4-015 is ABSENT from the 217755 parts list. The as-drawn bushing at this joint is Joby 214943-002 (BUSHING, PLAIN, ALUMINUM BRONZE, .250" ID), balloon 28 in DETAIL X.

No bearing balloon in DETAIL X -- internal to 208510-007 VARIABLE PITCH ACTUATOR ASSEMBLY (balloon 1). The workbook's comment column names MS21299C4K on this row, but that part is a countersunk washer (see column_I_caveat).

elements.name: bushing flange thickness
elements.note: 0.062 in -0.005/-0. Identical treatment to the tan-link stack's flange.

elements.name: pitch flange thickness
elements.note: Value + tolerance traced to 215197, but WHICH feature is ambiguous -- see source_ref. This is the clearest example in the workbook of why feature identity, not just value matching, is needed.

export.note: Established 2026-08-06 by handoff citation_export_provenance. This is the ONLY export of 215197 anywhere in the workspace: all three drawing-checker runs of it record this same sha256 in data/runs.jsonl, 20260730_133912's 215197_A_p01.json records source_pdf '[PRELIM 2025-MAY-22] 215197 A.1.pdf', and no other 215197 PDF exists in drawing-checker's inbox or fixtures. Unlike 217755 (six exports on disk), 'which export' has a unique answer here. This element's own note, unlike its tan_link sibling's, does not name the export it was read on -- so the basis here is uniqueness (there is only one 215197 export for 'sheet 2 zone D10' to refer to), not a written record of the reading.

source_ref.note: 215197 carries TWO 4.06 ±0.10 callouts: '5X 4.06 ±0.10' at sheet 2 zone D10 (perpendicularity 0.05 G, 5X INDIVIDUALLY) and a single '4.06 ±0.10' at sheet 1 zone D5 (positional 0.2 A B C, datum D). The workbook's 3.96/4.16 matches both. This joint is qty 1, which argues for the sheet-1 D5 callout; the tolerance alone cannot decide. Separately, DETAIL X balloons the VPA (1) against the TANGENTIAL LINK MOUNT 215175-002 (72), not the pitch plate 215177-001 -- so 215197 may be the wrong part entirely for this flange.

paths.label: total stack under the fastener grip

checks.label: worst case (MMC+ = max shank out)
checks.guidance: Grip minus the clamped stack. Negative at minimum means the thread run-out is pulled inside the joint; positive at maximum means full-diameter shank protrudes past the nut face. This stack has NO thread-transition allowance, unlike the tan-link take 1.

notes: The as-drawn joint is a castellated nut (MS9363-10, balloon 25) + cotter pin (MS24665-229, balloon 26). Grip length alone cannot answer this joint: the binding constraint is whether a castellation slot lines up with the cotter hole. The workbook does not model it; neither does this transcription.
This stack has no thread-transition element and no second washer branch, so it has strictly less modelling than the tan-link take 1.
